title: ADR: Model ABI and Runtime Stub Protocol
author: Alex Chen
content:
Summary
-------
This ADR defines a lightweight, versioned Model ABI (Application Binary Interface) plus a minimal runtime "stub" handshake protocol to enable safe deployment, graceful fallback, and automated compatibility checks between model artifacts and Redwood serving runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to reduce runtime failures due to subtle model packaging changes, allow automated routing to compatible variants, and simplify rollbacks and canaries for model updates.

Context and motivation
----------------------
Problem: model artifacts evolve (vocab changes, tokenizer metadata, kv-cache layout, quantization metadata, custom ops). These changes can cause runtime errors, degraded outputs, or silent correctness regressions when a model variant is served on an incompatible runtime or kernel configuration. Current mitigations (manual checklists and ad-hoc adapters) are error-prone and slow.

Goals:
- Provide a compact, machine-verified compatibility surface between model artifact and runtime.
- Allow the router/orchestrator to make deterministic compatibility decisions (route, convert, fallback).
- Surface incompatibilities early (pre-warm checks, health probes, or dry-run handshakes).
- Ensure safe rollouts and predictable fallbacks across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Non-goals:
- This ADR does not attempt to define a universal model file format. It targets the serving-time compatibility contract between an artifact and Redwood runtimes.

Decision
--------
We adopt a two-part contract: (1) a Model ABI manifest embedded with or alongside the model artifact describing stable capability keys and versioned fields, and (2) a lightweight runtime stub handshake (JSON-over-HTTP/gRPC) used at load-time and optionally during warmup to validate compatibility and enumerate supported capabilities.

Key decisions:
- Model ABI is a small, signed JSON manifest (manifest.json) that includes a capability vector, ABI version, public build hash, and optional normalized capability descriptors.
- ABI versions are semantic but strictly monotonic for breaking changes (major.minor.patch). Major increments indicate breaking ABI changes requiring orchestration-level migration. Minor increments indicate additive capabilities compatible with older runtimes. Patch increments are metadata fixes.
- Runtime stub handshake is a single RPC: CheckModelCompatibility(manifest) -> CompatibilityReport. The report is deterministic and includes flags: compatible, best_effort_compatible, requires_adapter, incompatible.
- Runtimes must implement a stable capability matcher library; orchestrator uses matching rules (table below) to decide route/fallback.

Specification (manifest fields)
------------------------------
The manifest is JSON, required keys only where noted. A canonical example is in Appendix A. Required fields:
- abi_version: string (semver)
- model_id: string (unique artifact id)
- model_hash: string (sha256)
- tokenizer_schema: string (short id, e.g., "bpe-v2")
- kv_cache_layout: string (e.g., "chunked-v1", "flat-v2")
- op_extensions: [string] (list of operator extension tags, may be empty)
- quantization_profile: string (e.g., "q8_0", "f16", "int8-symmetric")
- declared_max_sequence: string (integer as string)
- entrypoint_signature: string (stable descriptor for expected input/output shapes)
- signed_by: string (optional signer id)
- signature: string (optional detached signature, base64)

Compatibility evaluation rules (high-level)
-------------------------------------------
The runtime's CompatibilityReport is computed deterministically by matching manifest fields with the runtime's capability database and supported kernel paths:
- If abi_version.major > runtime_supported_major => incompatible.
- If tokenizer_schema mismatch => requires_adapter (tokenization shim) unless runtime has tokenizer plugin listed in op_extensions.
- If kv_cache_layout mismatch and model declares > 512 tokens for typical prefix usages => incompatible unless runtime advertises a compatible evictor.
- Quantization mismatch: if runtime supports at least the declared quantization_profile => compatible; otherwise best_effort_compatible if an acceptable fallback profile is available (e.g., runtime supports f16 for q8_0) but with a declared performance/quality delta.
- op_extensions: missing op extension => requires_adapter if an adapter exists; otherwise incompatible.

Report shape (fields in CompatibilityReport)
- compatible: true|false
- compatibility_level: one of ["full", "best_effort", "adapter_required", "incompatible"]
- adapters_available: [string] (names of known adapters on runtime)
- estimated_latency_multiplier: string (float as string, e.g., "1.12")
- quality_delta_estimate: string (percent change as string, e.g., "-0.5%")
- notes: string (human readable explanation)

Runtime stub protocol (load-time handshake)
-------------------------------------------
- For hosted and dedicated runtimes we use a gRPC endpoint: RuntimeService.CheckModelCompatibility(Manifest) returns CompatibilityReport. Private deployments may configure an HTTP/JSON compatibility endpoint to remain firewall-friendly.
- Handshake must be idempotent and cheap: no full model load, only metadata checks and optionally a fast dry-run using an isolated preloaded kernel set.
- The orchestrator will call the handshake during: pre-deploy validation, node-prewarm, and periodic liveness checks for pinned variants.

Operational semantics and rollout policy
--------------------------------------
1) Preflight: model artifact publishing pipeline must run a static manifest validation and simulate CheckModelCompatibility against a staging fleet. Results are published as part of the model’s release notes.
2) Canary: orchestrator marks a new model variant as canary if compatibility_level != "incompatible". Canary traffic limited to 0.5–2% or 1000 requests/day (whichever is smaller) for first 24–48 hours.
3) Gradual increase: if telemetry (see below) shows no regressions the orchestrator will ramp to 25% then 100% over configurable windows. Major ABI changes (major > previous) require a coordinator-approved migration and a forced compatibility gate.
4) Fallbacks: on detection of runtime-side errors attributed to model incompatibility the orchestrator will route to last-known-good variant and mark the new variant as failed.

Telemetry and SLO integration
---------------------------
Instrument the compatibility workflow with the following metrics (prometheus names suggested):
- redwood_model_compatibility_check_total{result="full"|"best_effort"|"adapter_required"|"incompatible"}
- redwood_model_compatibility_latency_seconds (histogram)
- redwood_model_fallbacks_total{reason="compat_mismatch"|"runtime_error"}
- redwood_model_quality_regression_alerts_total (triggered by eval harness)

SLO implications:
- Model compatibility gate is considered part of the deployment preflight; failures here block rollout.
- Fallbacks due to incompatibility are classified as degrade events for the model serving SLO with a high-weighted impact (operator must acknowledge and run postmortem if >3 fallbacks in 24h).

Security and signing
--------------------
- All manifests must be signed by the model release pipeline using an internal signing key. Runtimes validate signature when signature present; unsigned manifests are allowed only for internal dev clusters (flagged).
- Signing uses RFC 7515-style JWS or a simple detached signature with signer id included in manifest.
- Manifest signing prevents accidental substitution of ABI metadata in transit and is part of model-provenance requirements. See related model-artifact-provenance standard.

Alternative considered and rejected
----------------------------------
1) Heavyweight schema: full protobuf schema with binary encoding. Rejected because it increases packaging overhead for small artifacts and complicates ad-hoc inspection; JSON manifest is easier to audit and evolve.
2) No manifest, runtime introspection only. Rejected because runtime introspection requires loading large artifacts and risks causing degraded nodes during validation.
3) Single monolithic model format. Rejected as out-of-scope for the platform; too disruptive to the upstream model community.

Testing and verification
------------------------
- Unit tests for capability matcher must include a mutation matrix: change each manifest field and validate expected report class.
- Integration tests: a model pipeline publishes artifact+manifest to staging; orchestrator executes CheckModelCompatibility against a staging runtime and asserts deterministic routing.
- Regression harness: nightly runs which re-check compatibility of pinned production variants against latest runtime images. Any change in compatibility_level triggers an automated ticket.

Rollout checklist (for model owners)
-----------------------------------
1) Ensure manifest.json present and signed.
2) Run local compatibility verifier (redwood-cli model verify-manifest) against target runtime images.
3) Publish to staging and confirm CompatibilityReport == "full" or linked adapter exists.
4) Open canary release and monitor telemetry for 48h.
5) Promote or roll back per telemetry.

Owners and responsibilities
--------------------------
- Model artifact producers: produce accurate manifest and attach signatures.
- Runtime team: implement capability matcher and CheckModelCompatibility endpoint; publish capability catalog.
- Orchestrator team: integrate compatibility gate into deployment pipeline and implement fallback routing.
- Security: manage signing keys and rotate as described in model-provenance standard.

Open questions
--------------
- Adapter discovery: how to package and distribute adapters securely across private deployments? Suggestion: adapters packaged as signed container images and referenced by name in the manifest adapters_available list.
- Quality delta estimation: initial implementation will be conservative heuristic; extend by hooking in lightweight evals during canary.

Appendix A — Example manifest (manifest.json)
-------------------------------------------
{
  "abi_version": "1.2.0",
  "model_id": "redwood/gptx-mini-0312",
  "model_hash": "sha256:3f5a9d...",
  "tokenizer_schema": "bpe-v2",
  "kv_cache_layout": "chunked-v1",
  "op_extensions": ["rotary-pos-embed", "custom-norm-v1"],
  "quantization_profile": "q8_0",
  "declared_max_sequence": "8192",
  "entrypoint_signature": "text->tokens->logits",
  "signed_by": "release-pipeline-1",
  "signature": "BASE64(SIG)"
}

Appendix B — Compatibility handshake (gRPC / pseudocode)
--------------------------------------------------------
service RuntimeService {
  rpc CheckModelCompatibility(Manifest) returns (CompatibilityReport);
}

// pseudocode client usage
manifest = read('manifest.json')
report = runtimeClient.CheckModelCompatibility(manifest)
if report.compatibility_level == 'incompatible':
  abort_deploy(report.notes)
elif report.compatibility_level == 'adapter_required':
  if orchestrator.has_adapter(report.adapters_available):
    schedule_adapter_install(report.adapters_available[0])
  else:
    abort_deploy('No adapter available')
else:
  proceed_with_canary()

Appendix C — Compatibility matrix (example decision table)
---------------------------------------------------------
| Condition                          | Outcome          | Action |
| abi_major > runtime_major          | incompatible     | block  |
| tokenizer mismatch + no plugin     | adapter_required | fail-canary  |
| quant_profile unsupported but fallback available | best_effort | canary-with-warning |
| op_extension missing + no adapter  | incompatible     | block  |

Notes and future work
---------------------
- Over time we expect the ABI manifest to grow small optional fields (e.g., per-layer quant metadata). We must retain strict major-versioning discipline when making breaking changes.
- For private deployments, we will provide a lightweight schema validator CLI and optionally an agent that performs on-prem compatibility checks during upgrades.

Approval
--------
This ADR was approved by the Runtime and Orchestration leads on 2025-03-30 and is targeted for implementation in the 2025-Q2 runtime release.
